newsitem.title: POLAND: Two Poles face trial for communist-era hijacking.
newsitem.headline: Two Poles face trial for communist-era hijacking.

text.p: Two men who hijacked a Polish LOT airliner from communist Poland 15 years ago were formally indicted on Monday, the Warsaw prosecutor's office said.

"The accused, Marian P. and Jerzy Z., together with eight others hijacked to West Berlin a Soviet-built Antonov-24 LOT passenger plane on a scheduled internal flight," PAP news agency quoted prosecutor's spokesman Ryszard Kucinski as saying.
After the plane landed in West Berlin, only a handful of passengers agreed to return to Poland, then under military rule. The remaining 35 refused.
In December 1981, communist leader Wojciech Jaruzelski had clamped the country under martial to crush the defiant Solidarity movement, then the Soviet bloc's only free trade union.
If convicted, the hijackers could face jail terms of up to eight years.
"Their crime was not subject to any amnesty because it was not politically motivated, nor had they been persecuted (in Poland)," Kucinski said.
He said the prosecutor's office reopened the case after accidentally realising that Jerzy Z. had returned to Poland after several years abroad.
